category: the most overrated album of all time

a.claim: "You have spent a quarter-century mistaking whiny suburban technophobia and bloated art-rock dirges for profound existential philosophy."
a.check: The album's release date — OK Computer came out in 1997, so a quarter-century only holds if the claim is made from 2022 onward.

b.check: An isolated vocal track of Yoko Ono run through a waveform analyzer against the shrieking spectrum of a wounded mammal to see if it’s genuine affect or just uncalibrated mic-peaking.

c.claim: You have spent a quarter-century mistaking whiny suburban technophobia and bloated art-rock dirges for profound existential philosophy.
c.check: I would check the album's total runtime against the standard definition of a "dirge" to verify if its 53-minute length objectively constitutes bloat.

b.says: Checking the release date shows the album has indeed been out for over a quarter-century today, while evaluating its 53-minute runtime against standard rock pacing demonstrates that the sprawling, sluggish compositions qualify as bloated dirges.

a.pick: The Dark Side of the Moon
a.why: It's a technical marvel, sure, but it's background music for people who want to feel deep — the needle-drop is the personality.
a.raw:
PICK: The Dark Side of the Moon
BECAUSE: It's a technical marvel, sure, but it's background music for people who want to feel deep — the needle-drop is the personality.

b.why: You have spent a quarter-century mistaking whiny suburban technophobia and bloated art-rock dirges for profound existential philosophy.
b.raw:
PICK: Radiohead's OK Computer
BECAUSE: You have spent a quarter-century mistaking whiny suburban technophobia and bloated art-rock dirges for profound existential philosophy.

c.why: You mistake raw, primal vulnerability for amateurish noise.
c.raw:
PICK: Yoko Ono’s Plastic Ono Band
BECAUSE: You mistake raw, primal vulnerability for amateurish noise.

a.why: Neither defence moved me; b’s “raw, primal vulnerability” for Yoko Ono sounds like special pleading, and c’s attack on OK Computer as “whiny suburban technophobia” is vivid but doesn’t make Dark Side any less overplayed or overcanonized.

b.why: Neither defense dismantled the sanctified cultural pedestal surrounding *OK Computer*, as calling Yoko's shrieks "vulnerability" fails to prove her widely reviled record is overrated, and nobody excused Radiohead's bloated, whiny dirges.

c.why: The critiques failed to dismantle my view that the album's raw vulnerability is authentic rather than technically flawed or overrated.
